claims.experiment: Used HCO+ abundance and a reduced chemical network to infer the ionization fraction, then evaluated magnetic Reynolds number and Am
claims.result: R_e > 1e6 and Am < 0.1 with zeta ~ 1e-17 s^-1 at n = 1e6 cm^-3
claims.finding: MRI is likely not active in the observed molecular layer; other mechanisms (winds, GI, hydrodynamical instabilities) are needed

evidence.quote: find values that imply that the accretion process is not driven by the magneto-rotational instability

evidence.loc: 5.3 Accretion processes in a young disk
evidence.quote: MRI is likely not active in the observed molecular layer

claims.hypothesis: The disk orientation can be constrained from resolved dust continuum
claims.experiment: Gaussian intensity profile fits to continuum visibilities at five frequencies with GALARIO and emcee
claims.result: Inclination 50 +/- 3 deg and position angle about 75-76 deg
claims.finding: The dust disk is detected at 203-260 GHz and its orientation is tightly constrained

evidence.quote: $i=50^{\circ} \pm 3^{\circ}$ and $PA = 76^{\circ} \pm 4^{\circ}$

claims.hypothesis: The molecular abundances of the young disk resemble those of Class II disks but differ from Solar System objects
claims.experiment: Compared derived abundances and ratios with Class II disks and comets/Titan from the literature
claims.result: Similar to the envelope and Class II disks; discrepancies relative to Solar System objects
claims.finding: Differences trace chemical evolution during disk and planet formation

evidence.quote: The molecular abundances averaged over the TMC1A disk are similar to its protostellar envelope and other, older Class II disks. We meanwhile find a discrepancy between the young disk’s molecular abundances relative to Solar System objects.

claims.hypothesis: Resolved HCN emission can be assigned to disk or envelope components
claims.experiment: Compared HCN spectra, channel maps and moment maps with CO isotopolog and HCO+ emission
claims.result: Two HCN peaks: west (red-shifted, co-spatial with disk tracers) and north (outflow cavity wall)
claims.finding: The western red-shifted HCN comes from the surface of the Keplerian disk; the northern emission traces envelope near the outflow cavity wall

evidence.quote: Two HCN emission peaks are located to the west on the red-shifted side of the disk and to the north of the blue-shifted side of the disk.

claims.hypothesis: The DCN/HCN ratio in the TMC1A disk can be constrained
claims.experiment: Proxy-masked spectra and column densities from the HCN and DCN 3-2 lines
claims.result: DCN not detected; DCN/HCN < 0.3 (< 0.26 for 8-10 km/s)
claims.finding: Upper limits are consistent with other young stellar objects and Solar System objects

evidence.loc: 5.2 Molecular abundances in the TMC1A disk.
evidence.quote: Our upper limits to the DCN/HCN fraction in the TMC1A disk are, meanwhile, consistent with other various young stellar objects and Solar System objects.

why_this_data.value: TMC1A has a favorable inclination and simple geometry with a well-defined disk, making it a laboratory for the abundances of simple molecules on ~15 au scales

evidence.quote: The relatively simple geometry of TMC1A with its well-defined disk, makes it an ideal laboratory for determining the distribution and abundances of common, simple molecules

why_this_method.value: Optically thin LTE column densities as a zeroth-order estimate, checked with non-LTE radiative transfer

evidence.loc: 4.1 Molecular column density of the disk
evidence.quote: To zeroth order, the molecular column density of the emitting gas can be determined by assuming a thermalized, optically thin layer of emission

referee_caveats_inferred: Abundances rest on one assumed Tex (30 K) and a CO abundance of 1e-4 with ISM isotopic ratios; uncertainties are quoted only as ranges spanning orders of magnitude
No formal error budget for column densities; by-eye temperature profile
Strong spatial filtering (about 90% of CO-isotopolog flux lost vs lower resolution) biases abundance ratios, especially SO/CO
Disk/envelope separation is qualitative (spectra and moment maps), not from a physical model
PA quoted as 75 in Sect. 3.1 and 76 in Summary; HCO+ frequency in text (267.8527) differs from the table (267.5576)

missing_for_reproduction: Briggs robust, clean parameters, masks and taper details
Self-calibration parameters and line-free channel ranges
Calibrator flux values and first-data-set processing (deferred to earlier papers)
RADEX grids and linewidths, binning for azimuthal averages
Envelope and Solar System comparison values used in the abundance figure
No stated public release of scripts or reduced products
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Seven ALMA long-baseline execution blocks over three projects; roughly 100-300 GB raw, 20-60 GB calibrated measurement sets
reproducibility.score_reason: Three ALMA projects are named and the continuum fitting recipe and column-density method are described with numeric results, but imaging settings (robust, masks, cleaning), self-calibration details and key comparison values are missing or deferred to earlier papers.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Project codes are given but the data release status is not stated in the paper and the imaging and self-calibration recipe is too incomplete to redo the line cubes and flux densities exactly.

methods_papers.why: Imaging and calibration of the first ALMA data set and the phase center
NOEMA data processing and the water upper limit
Reduced chemical network for the HCO+ and ionization calculation

companion_papers.why: Earlier publication of the 2015.1.01549.S CO data and disk wind
Earlier Keplerian disk analysis of TMC1A
Earlier lower-resolution molecular and continuum study of TMC1A
Recent observations also indicating lack of CO freeze-out in the TMC1A disk
